A1.justification: Both complete 31-page PDFs describe the same PairFlow work. The main text, Appendices A–K, equations, tables, and figures are readable and can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular and image generation experiments in Section 5, with numerical results in Appendix D. Its appendices also report continuous-flow, synthetic-data, FFHQ, LM1B, and supplementary analysis results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the molecular and image comparisons, continuous-flow experiments, larger-domain evaluations, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4, Equations 9–12, and Algorithm 1 retain the same closed-form pairing procedure. The continuous-flow variant in Appendix E and subset-pairing adaptation in Appendix H are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate QM9, ZINC-250k, MNIST-Binary, CIFAR-10, FFHQ, LM1B, continuous-valued MNIST, and dimension-varying two-moons data. All these tasks and scenarios already appear in v1, including its appendices.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments: MDLM, UDLM, Random pairing, DCD/ReDi variants, and continuous-domain CondOT/ReFlow comparisons are retained. Correcting the ReFlow citation does not introduce a different comparison method.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, sampling budgets, preprocessing, training configurations, and reference datasets are unchanged. Section 5.1 retains 1,024 molecular samples, 1,000 images for MNIST-Binary FID, and 5,000 images for CIFAR-10 evaluation; the appendix protocols also match.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same forward-sampling coverage and total-correlation analyses, dimensionality study, iterative re-flow experiments, subset-pairing study, and overfitting/memorization checks in Appendices C, E, G, H, and J.

E5.justification: The molecular results retain the same ten-trial or ten-run mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Appendices D, G, and H. Appendix C.2 also retains its varying-seed total-correlation estimation procedure. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted findings, and qualitative samples are unchanged throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 6 reports one-step QM9 validity of 223.4 ± 12.7 for PairFlow and 17.5 ± 3.2 for UDLM in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, and derivations are unchanged, including the discrete velocity proofs in Appendix A and continuous-flow derivation in Appendix E.1. Section 3.2 repairs citations without revising its mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: teacher-free source–target pairing, preprocessing costing up to 1.7% of base training, competitive few-step generation, and stronger initialization for subsequent distillation.

C2.justification: The explanations involving dataset coverage and total correlation, the hypothesis about poor CIFAR-10 distillation performance, and the overfitting interpretation are retained. Appendix K keeps the same qualification about diminishing benefits for higher-dimensional continuous data.

D1.justification: The hyperparameters, CUDA implementation disclosure, greedy-tail sampling, RTX A6000 timings, and continuous-flow and language-model training details remain unchanged. No implementation or code/data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged. 'Xingchao et al., 2023' and 'Liu et al., 2023' identify the same rectified-flow paper. The Chelba reference retains its authors and arXiv identifier while its title is revised; these are bibliographic repairs.

P1.justification: v2 replaces unresolved question-mark citations in Section 3.2 and Appendix G with Liu et al. (2023), corrects ReFlow author-name rendering throughout, and revises the Chelba reference title. These are limited editorial corrections; the narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Citation corrections cause limited text reflow and bibliography rearrangement: the rectified-flow entry moves from page 11 to page 10, and DINOv2 moves from page 10 to page 11. All figures, tables, and Algorithm 1 retain their displays and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves broken citations in Section 3.2 and Appendix G and improves the bibliography's author-name and title information. This makes attribution clearer and references easier to identify, providing a limited editorial quality improvement. The scientific methods, evidence, claims, and limitations remain unchanged.
